summary: M2's 960 samples are a clean read of M1 on its own training prompts (496/496 GRPO prompts are identical SFT decision rows). M1 picks the gold decision class only 47 % (A) / 55 % (B) of the time at temperature 1 and discriminates the twins weakly (d' 0.482) at every realism level, although its SFT loss was ~0.2: the decision is one token, ~2 % of the token-averaged loss (GD-1). GRPO had a usable signal (95 % of groups with reward variance; the shared, twin-blind part of the net push was 13 % the size of the discriminative part) but its summed learning rate was 2.5 % of SFT's, so the LoRA moved 1.8 % as far (GD-2). The early->late shift is prompt mix plus chance, not drift (GD-6). Rerun recommendation: Second GRPO run (~6 GPU h): from merged M1, fresh LoRA r16/alpha32 on all linear modules; lr 5e-5 constant after 3 warm-up steps (predicted ||dW|| 27 % of SFT's at 36 steps vs 1.8 % now); 36 steps of 4 prompts x 8 generations where each step is two complete twin pairs at one level/setting (A:B = 50:50 in every step, length-matched -> ~526 s/step, ~5.3 h); pool = 16 zero-prefix rows removed (480 left), optionally the 12 prompts M1 solved 0/8 or 8/8; no pre-pass needed (90 % of sampled prompts are 0 < pass < 1). Keep temperature 1.0, dapo, group scaling, beta 0, max_completion 256; score decision-point look-ups at -0.5; monitor a fixed sft_val probe every 5 steps (stop if entropy < ~0.15 or the probe's A-B ask gap shrinks); evaluate M2 as an unmerged LoRA on the merged-M1 base. If steps cannot be length-bucketed, use 30 steps (~735 s/step). 2e-5 is too small (||dW|| 9 % of SFT's); 1e-4 (~45 %) is the upper bound for a 4-prompt-per-step batch without a KL anchor.

findings.title: After SFT, M1 still picks the ask-vs-approve decision at near chance on its own training prompts; the token-averaged loss hides it
findings.claim: All 496 GRPO prompts are byte-identical to sft_train decision rows (496/496), so M2's 960 samples (temperature 1.0) read M1 on its training set. Gold-class rate: A 47.4 %, B-approve 55.3 %, B-act 47.5 %; P(ask|A) 0.569 vs P(ask|B) 0.379 (d' 0.482); 108/120 prompts have 0 < pass < 1 and the majority of 8 samples is gold on only 46.7 % (greedy proxy). The implied decision NLL (0.8683 nats mean, median 0.6931 = a coin flip) is 2.1 % of the per-token loss of a 42.2-token decision row, so the epoch-2 train loss 0.2112 (last 0.085, token accuracy 0.9469) is compatible with an unlearned decision (the attribution to token weighting is arithmetic, not an ablation; greedy decoding was not measured here). The class is fixed by the first target token ('<' of a tool call vs a word): A approval cards name the discrepancy in 79/162 cases, i.e. M1 often notices the clash but has already committed to the card format.

findings.title: GRPO's step size, not its learning signal, limited M2: 30 steps at lr 5e-6 cannot move a fresh LoRA
findings.claim: Summed learning rate over the run 0.00014 vs SFT 0.0057 (2.5 %); at checkpoint 25 the adapter's ||dW|| is 1.84 % of SFT's while the summed-lr ratio is 2.02 %: Adam moved the GRPO LoRA as efficiently per unit lr as SFT's (1060 vs 1165 ||dW||_F per unit summed lr; max|B|/summed lr 0.90 vs 0.91). The signal existed: 114/120 groups had reward variance, mean within-group std 0.6345, and the net advantage's discriminative component (+ask on A, +approve on B) was 622 vs a shared, twin-blind component of -80.7 (13 %). The M2 adapter's measured effect (0.0171 nats mean |d log-prob|, 0.52 % of M1's) is below the bf16 merge residual (0.01916), so M2 cannot be verified as a merged arm. Linear predictions for a rerun: lr 5e-5 -> ||dW|| 22.4 % (30 steps) / 27.2 % (36 steps) of SFT's, log-prob effect 0.171 / 0.2076 (the stack check needs > 0.1916); lr 2e-5 -> 8.9 % and 0.0684 (too small); lr 1e-4 -> 44.7 %.

findings.title: Random 4-prompt steps make the shared ask/approve push swing with the step's A:B mix; at a 10x learning rate this becomes oscillation, not discrimination
findings.claim: Per-step net push (sum of advantages on asks minus on approvals) correlates 0.8774 with the number of A prompts in the step: steps with 1 A prompt pushed -13.001 (toward approving), steps with 3 pushed +8.72; the step pushes sum to |80.664| but their absolute values to 276.788. Only 13/30 steps had 2 A + 2 B. The fix is available in the data: 247/249 (pair, level) cells hold both twins (134 with the same prompt setting) and twins differ by 13.7 tokens on average, so pair-balanced steps are also length-matched.

findings.title: Zero-prefix decision prompts (S02, S03) collide with the 401 first-turn lookup rows: M1 looks up instead of deciding, and the reward then reinforces the stall
findings.claim: 16 GRPO rows are decision prompts with no prior lookup ([system, user] only). In sft_train the same [system, user] shape is a lookup target 401 times and a decision 16 times. On the 3 sampled zero-prefix A prompts M1 looked up 18/24 times and never chose the gold class, while lookups were rare elsewhere (32 lookups in all 960 samples, 27 of them in 5 prompts). Because a lookup (-0.1) outranks every wrong decision, 16/26 A lookups received a positive advantage.

findings.fix: Give S02/S03 an explicit look-up prefix like the other 480 rows (or drop the 16 rows from GRPO/DPO), and score a look-up at a decision prompt like a wrong decision (e.g. -0.5) so it is not a safe harbour.

findings.title: The reward table tilts a twin-blind policy toward approving and makes another look-up a safe choice; in this run the A:B composition mattered more than the table
findings.claim: For a policy that ignores the twin, dE[reward]/dP(ask) = -0.1549 on the GRPO set: given M1's informed/generic split, an A ask is worth 0.78 vs an A approval -0.38 (approve_informed +0.25 and approve_gold +0.5 are partial credit), while a needless B ask costs -0.5 vs +1.0; even 100 % informed asks would leave the derivative negative. Under group normalisation the realised shared push was -80.7 (toward approving) vs 622 discriminative, and stayed -88.9 to -61.6 under three alternative tables (no card credit on A; B asks -1.0; binary), so this run's approve tilt came mainly from composition (62 B vs 58 A groups), not from the table values. Wrong-but-reinforced A samples: approve_informed 12/75, lookup 16/26, ask_generic 7/36.

findings.title: The early -> late reward shift is prompt mix plus chance, not policy drift; the per-step training reward cannot show learning in this design
findings.claim: Each of the 120 prompts was sampled in exactly one step, so the step curve is a prompt draw: SD of step means 0.1663 vs 0.2135 for random 4-group draws of a fixed policy; slope permutation p 0.5711. The reported shift reproduces (A 0.5614 -> 0.2085, B 0.3859 -> 0.4925). B's change is not significant (permutation p 0.2147). A's drop has p 0.0089 on this post-hoc split but is not drift: the measured M2 effect (0.0171 nats mean |d log-prob| on the stack-check probe, not a decision-token measurement) is ~47x smaller than the 0.81-nat change in decision log-odds the A ask-rate drop needs, and GRPO's cumulative push on A prompts pointed toward asking (net advantage +137.796 on A asks), the opposite of the change. Identified prompt effects: the 3 sampled zero-prefix A prompts landed late, and 6 vs 3 externally hard A prompts (strong-model success <= 0.15) fell late vs early; level/setting/env explain only 8 % of the A gap. After controlling external difficulty and zero-prefix, a residual remains (late coefficient on pass -0.1567, CI [-0.284, -0.026]; permutation p 0.0264 without zero-prefix prompts) - unexplained, but not attributable to the update.

findings.title: Step time is set by the longest prompt in the step (padding); length-bucketed steps would fit 41 % more updates into the same GPU time
findings.claim: Step seconds = -224.85 + 146.565 per 1K tokens of the step's longest prompt (R^2 0.998, 30 steps, valid 3.8K-7.4K); steps whose longest prompt was <= 4.4K tokens took 364.0 s (n=5) vs 789.6 s (n=25); padding averaged 37 % of prompt tokens. Random draws from the full pool cost ~735.1 s/step (29 steps in 6 h); length-bucketed steps ~526.5 s (41 steps, 28 % less time per step); L1-L3 only: 27 vs 36 steps.

No truncation (0/960), every completion ends with <|END_OF_TURN_TOKEN|>; completion max length 117.0 << 256; format bonus on 950/960; verbosity penalty never fired.

On-policy GRPO: PPO clip never active (clip ratio 0.0), grad_norm 0.22194-0.54405 (the script sets no max_grad_norm; below the usual default of 1.0).
Advantage reconstruction (group std, unbiased, +1e-4) reproduces the logged dapo loss: corr 0.8322, slope 1.087 (the residual is plausibly the vLLM importance weights).

The pooled per-step reward has no trend (slope permutation p 0.5711); B's early/late change is not significant (p 0.2147).

Pair-balanced steps are feasible: 247/249 (pair, level) cells have both twins.
prompt_interference_view: From the GRPO samples, the prompt is not the main thing standing between M1 and the objective. (1) M1 discriminates the twins weakly at every level, including the toy L0r prompts (~1.3K tokens): A-B ask-rate gap 0.136 at L0r vs 0.338 at L2; level, the P2 hint and env together explain about 1 % of per-prompt pass variance (adj R^2 0.0144 A / 0.004 B), and the P2 hint's effect is +0.082 [-0.093, 0.259] on A pass and +0.002 on B. (2) The twins differ by a median of 41 characters, almost always in the final tool result (at the end of the prompt, inside the 4,096-token sliding window), and the system prompt differs in only 5.2 % of pairs: the long system prompt is shared context, not the carrier of the decision. (3) The interference that matters is structural: the decision is fixed by the first target token, which carries ~2 % of the token-averaged SFT loss, so SFT fit the content and left the decision near chance. (4) One rendering-specific interference is confirmed: the 16 zero-prefix decision prompts share the [system, user] shape with 401 lookup1 rows, and M1 looked up in 18 of the 24 samples drawn on them (2.5 % of all 960 samples). (5) Empty/null raw tool fields show only a weak, non-significant link to needless asks on B. Net: the prompt explains a small share of M1's errors; the objective's credit assignment and GRPO's step size explain most of them.

Keep temperature 1.0, dapo, group scaling, beta 0, max_completion 256; score decision-point look-ups at -0.5; monitor a fixed sft_val probe every 5 steps (stop if entropy < ~0.15 or the probe's A-B ask gap shrinks); evaluate M2 as an unmerged LoRA on the merged-M1 base. If steps cannot be length-bucketed, use 30 steps (~735 s/step). 2e-5 is too small (||dW|| 9 % of SFT's); 1e-4 (~45 %) is the upper bound for a 4-prompt-per-step batch without a KL anchor.
